newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Part of Siberian grain harvest under snow.
newsitem.headline: Part of Siberian grain harvest under snow.

text.p: Many farms in Siberia have stopped harvesting grain due to snows and a shortage of equipment, which could push Russia's net grain output even further below expectations.

Interfax news agency quoted Ivan Gridasov, head of the Agriculture Ministry's crops growing section, as saying that a shortage of equipment meant 360,000 hectares in Novosibirsk, 140,000 in Tomsk and 120,000 in Omsk had yet to be harvested.
Crops in the Kemerov, Krasnoyarsk and Altai regions were under snow, he said.
Russia had threshed 41.8 million hectares, or 87 percent, of the total area sown to crops this year, as of October 26.
Large farms had threshed 68.6 million tonnes gross of grain by that date.
State Statistics Committee figures for October 21, the last day for which data was available, put gross grain output on all farms at 73.5 million tonnes.
Russia, expecting a net grain harvest of around 70-72 million tonnes this year, had pinned its hopes on the Siberian harvest.
But output there has been hit by heavy rains and now snow.
